review_finding.claim: The FIXUP-4 text in W3-005 device_notes creates three 7-grams shared with W3-004. FIXUP-3 held them in W3-004 alone. Condition 3's clause 'no new 7-gram shared across rows from FIXUP-4 text' is not met.
review_finding.evidence: ngram7.py --gate 10 --full-ids on private 5x clones, so that two rows reach the gate and one row does not: grams 'measure w b over the rp and', 'w b over the rp and sblgnt', 'b over the rp and sblgnt texts' fire with rows W3-004, W3-005 on the FIXUP-4 clones and not on the FIXUP-3 clones. My own re-implementation returned the same grams. The bytes are what R5-S5-11 ordered, so the apply is correct.
review_finding.suggested_fix: Candidate wording for the controlling agent, since the text is byte-ordered: 'counts MEASURED by scripts measure_w3b and measure_w3 over'. It breaks the run with W3-004, and the grams then fall in the set W3-005 already shared in FIXUP-3. Tested only on a private variant, not on any row: ngram7 --gate 10 --full-ids on 5x clones showed 0 new shared 7-grams against FIXUP-3, and run_validator_suite.py gave hard_status GREEN, dead_members [] on the variant. Tiling and the CWO sweep were not run on the variant.
